review.description: S1 preserves immediate native completion and same-session follow-up while late workflow persistence failures become sanitized diagnostics for their originating completed turn. S3 interruption remains a single native terminal result, not a workflow-error diagnostic. S4 retains inactive versus acknowledged-active continuation state across storage failures after an answer.
review.implementation: Client records native terminal identity/status and reports only late workflow failure after successful interactive completion. It releases execution ownership before invoking the existing callback, preserving the Manager.Close lock boundary; generic app callback handling retains the diagnostic without new lifecycle state or replay authority. The question continuation owner restores idle only while admission remains starting, preserving active provider identity after acknowledgement and preserving terminal state.
review.tests: Inspected failure-store regressions for task/review/question-repair: original code misses the diagnostic; fixed code preserves one completed turn while turn-2 remains active, reports old identity with generic text, interrupts follow-up once and records exactly two starts. Separate simulated session-lock test proves Close returns before blocked callback delivery and callback exits after unlock; ordinary success/interruption/failure tests reject duplicate diagnostics. The two-case answered-continuation storage regression verifies pre-send idle/unclaimed state versus acknowledged running/identity, rejects false idle journal events despite queued native notifications, and proves no repeated turn after storage recovery.
